title: Panzanella
subtitle: tuscan bread and tomato salad
excerpt: Panzanella is a Tuscan salad made from stale bread soaked in water and tomato juices, then tossed with ripe tomatoes, basil, capers, and a sharp red wine vinegar dressing. The bread becomes the body of the salad rather than a garnish. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Panzanella is a dish from Tuscany, originally made by farmers and labourers to use up stale bread. The recipe is mentioned in Italian writing from as early as the 16th century. Today it is associated with summer eating in Tuscany.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best assembled 30 minutes before serving. Do not dress too far ahead or the bread will become waterlogged.

content.text: . salting the tomatoes and leaving them to sit so they release their juices, which then soak into the bread and become the dressing. The technique turns two simple ingredients into something considerably more than the sum of their parts. This recipe serves 4.
Use the best tomatoes you can find and properly stale bread. Fresh bread makes panzanella soggy and one-dimensional.

Tear or cut the stale bread into rough 3cm chunks. Place in a bowl and sprinkle with cold water . just enough to dampen it slightly but not make it wet. Leave for 5 minutes, then squeeze out most of the water with your hands. The bread should be moist but not dripping. Set aside.
Place the torn tomatoes in a large bowl. Add a pinch of flaky sea salt and toss. Leave for 15 minutes . the tomatoes will release a good amount of juice.
Add the squeezed bread to the tomatoes and toss to coat it in the tomato juices. Add the sliced onion and capers.
Drizzle over the red wine vinegar and olive oil. Toss well. Taste and adjust . the salad should be well-seasoned and sharp.
Leave to sit for at least 15 minutes before serving. Tear over the basil leaves just before plating and toss once more.

attrs.solution: You added too much water when soaking the bread, or the bread was too soft to start with. Use properly stale bread and squeeze very firmly after soaking. The bread should hold its shape.
Panzanella needs generous seasoning and good tomatoes. If the tomatoes are not sweet and ripe the salad will be flat. Use a little more vinegar and check the olive oil is good quality.
Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 minutes before adding to the salad. This removes much of the sharpness while leaving the flavour.

content.text: Panzanella comes from Tuscany. It is a summer salad eaten when tomatoes are at their best. The dish was originally eaten by farmworkers who soaked their stale bread in water and dressed it with whatever was in the field. Florence and Siena both claim it as their own. It is now widely known beyond Italy.
